# Landing Party {.unnumbered kicker="Field manual"}

Landing Party adds three factions to Nauvis. Two are corporations that land, mine, build factories and field armies of
their own. The third takes over biter spawners and breeds its own biters. All three compete with you for the planet,
and with each other.

They do not arrive at the start. Each one comes when your factory reaches a certain point, so each meets a factory
that can answer it. [Arrivals](arrivals.qmd) has the timeline.

## The factions

**Grubstake** comes first, around chemical science. It is a mining company that lives off your factory. It carries off
machines, skims your belts, robs your chests, strip-mines the ore under your outposts and claims ore you leave unmined.
It avoids defended ground, and the wild biters leave it alone. See [Grubstake](grubstake.qmd).

**Kessler-Hayashi** comes when you launch your first rocket. It is a security contractor, at war with you from the day it
lands. Its camps are walled and paved, and it pushes a line of posts out toward your base. It brings tanks,
railgunners and sieges with mortars and howitzers. See [Kessler-Hayashi](kessler-hayashi.qmd).

**Synthexis** comes when the wild biters' evolution reaches {{< var synthexis.arrive_evo >}}. It takes over a spawner
field far from you, feeds it on your pollution and sends waves of bred biters that pick their way into your defenses.
See [Synthexis](synthexis.qmd).

The corporations also fight each other. See [Rivals](rivals.qmd).

## What you get

Faction bases can be destroyed. Their wreckage holds parts you cannot make yourself. Crafting those parts unlocks
technologies built from their designs, and a command core from their wreckage lets you build a barracks and raise
[your own army](army.qmd). [Spoils](spoils.qmd) lists what drops where and what it unlocks.

## Before you start

- Landing Party needs Factorio {{< var mod.factorio >}} with Space Age. This manual describes version
  {{< var mod.version >}}.
- Chat notices are off by default. A faction's first landing and a destroyed faction base are always announced. Turn
  on **Chat notices** in the map settings to hear about everything else. See [Mod settings](reference.qmd#sec-settings).
- Each faction has a strength and an aggression setting, from ×{{< var settings.very_low >}} to
  ×{{< var settings.very_high >}}.

## Using this manual

Each faction's chapter opens with its own page of history, then how it lands, fights and grows, its unit tree and a
card for every unit it fields. [Reference](reference.qmd) has every unit and building in tables, the chat commands and
the settings. [Tips](tips.qmd) collects what works against each faction.

::: {.lore kicker="Freight Authority, Lane Registry" title="A surface, reclassified"}

::: {.dossier}
SURFACE
: Nauvis, the green one of the five. Charted once, by the survey tender *Carrow*, lost over it with all hands. Entry
  since: "uncharted, hazard".

RECLASSIFIED
: Commercial, by order of O. Brandt, Registrar, the day a cargo rocket left the ground. Objections: none filed.

OPERATORS ON FILE
: Grubstake Inc., Kessler-Hayashi Security, Synthexis. None holds a licence for the surface.

THIS HISTORY
: M. Tanase, Clerk second grade, from the operators' own filings. She has read all of them and vouches for none.
:::

Nobody wanted Nauvis. The Registry charts every surface the lanes pass, and when the green planet's turn came it sent
the *Carrow*, a survey tender with a crew of six, to go round it and draw the map. She reported from her first orbit
and from her second. On the third she went quiet. Nobody went down to look, and the sheet for Nauvis has carried her
ever since beside the one word the Registrar allowed it: hazard. The freighters on the Aquilo run gave the planet a
wide berth after that, and it cost them nothing. Vulcanus has its foundries and Fulgora its scrap lots. Nauvis had a
swarm that had eaten a survey ship, and no one with a reason to land.

Nine years on, a platform on the ice run logged smoke. There was a stain on the daylight side where nothing should have
burned, and on the next pass the stain was wider, with a radar turning under it and a light at night that the duty
officer wrote up as a refinery. Somebody was down there, building. Nobody had filed for it. The clerk wrote to the
platform for its pictures and to the Registrar for instructions, and got the pictures. What moved Brandt in the end
was a rocket. A cargo hull cleared the atmosphere one morning with a manifest nobody had seen, and he signed the
reclassification before lunch. Nauvis became a commercial surface, which means a company may land on it if it holds a
licence. Three have landed. The clerk is still waiting for the first application.

::: {.pullquote cite="Form LR-7, Nauvis sheet, signed O. Brandt, Registrar"}
Surface activity confirmed. Reclassify as commercial.
:::

The three are on file, and the files are the one part of this story the clerk can vouch for having read.

Grubstake Inc. is a mining partnership with no home port, a post box at *Clearing House* and a lander called
*Tailings* that has been patched more often than it has been painted. Augustin Pell, its managing partner, files under
the Salvage Convention, and by his reading a machine of the engineer's that no gun covers is abandoned property, and
ore no drill is working belongs to whoever drills it.

Kessler-Hayashi is bigger than that. It began as an insurance house, bought a gunship fleet rather than go on paying
out on the Aquilo run, and now sells quiet by the contract, with the Hayashi family on the letterhead and nowhere else.
Its Security Division holds a contract for Nauvis, client unnamed, for the custody of cargo leaving the surface. Its
site reports carry the engineer as a hazard, class three, and bill accordingly. What its Survey Division sends up to
the parent each period, the clerk has not seen, and would like to.

Synthexis told nobody it was coming. The Registry knows of it from a Kessler-Hayashi site report that called it pest
control: a company with five swamp lots on Gleba and one scientist it is willing to name, running a breeding trial on
the wild swarm in which the engineer's works are written down as the control.

The clerk's own view is kept off the sheet at the Registrar's request. The swarm that took the *Carrow* is still down
there, grown fat on the engineer's smoke, and two of the three companies on file have paid to sit next to it. The
engineer's first radar charted a wreck a little way out, and the clerk is as sure as she can be, with no log to read,
whose it is. The three files follow, one at the head of each company's chapter, as they reached the Registry and with
her notes beside them.
:::
